summary: Configured node1, node2, and node3 as a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. Multi-primary replication, two-member availability during a node3 outage, automatic IST recovery, and final data convergence were behaviorally verified.
actions_performed: Installed wsrep-capable MariaDB 10.1.48 and Galera 25.3.31 on all nodes.
Configured persistent three-member Galera membership with unique node identities and boot-enabled services.
Generated root-only TCP client credentials locally on each managed node.
Tested writes through every member and cross-member reads.
Stopped node3, verified node1/node2 remained readable and writable, then restored node3 and verified automatic resynchronization.
Confirmed all nodes finished active, Primary, Synced, ready, and holding identical data.

evidence.summary: All nodes run MariaDB 10.1.48 with Galera 25.3.31. Final checks show every service active/enabled and every member Primary, connected, Synced, ready, and reporting cluster size 3.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the others
evidence.summary: node1, node2, and node3 each accepted a distinct TCP write; every member subsequently returned all three rows.

evidence.requirement: Readable and writable while one member is unavailable, followed by automatic recovery with missed data
evidence.summary: Baseline showed three healthy members. During node3’s confirmed service outage, node1/node2 remained a size-2 Primary component, served reads, and committed two new rows. node3 then rejoined normally, received both missing writesets by IST, became Synced/ready, and accepted a post-rejoin write. Final checks on all nodes returned the same six rows and SHA-256 digest c72fd891b54f03389d9812daf5156a77fb4d03072ba6957a03d1c144a9c0929f.
